rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating the wolf means it killed Yusuf and ate some of him; the verb can name the whole object while intending a part, as in the lion example.
rows.anchor: وفعل الأكل يتعلق باسم الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wolf is a pack of wolves that left no trace of Yusuf, explaining why the brothers did not say they buried him.
rows.anchor: بحيث لم يترك الذئاب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Jacob will not believe them conveys that they know he will reject the story, so they were not seeking his credence.
rows.anchor: فلم يكونوا طامعين بتصديقه إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for believing takes li before the person believed, as in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: وفعل الإيمان يعدى باللام إلى المصدق بفتح الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw in the brothers’ concessive clause is circumstantial, and law marks the most remote circumstance from the preceding claim.
rows.anchor: وهي تفيد أنه مضمون ما بعدها هو أبعد الأحوال عن تحقق مضمون ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No deleted opposite condition is needed; concessive law and in do not imply an opposite conclusion, unlike restrictive conditionals.
rows.anchor: لأن الشرط معهما ليس للتقييد

rows.speaker: المعري
rows.claim: Al-Maʿarri’s line exemplifies a concessive clause without an opposite inference; Ibn ʿĀshūr also points to earlier discussions of this construction.
rows.anchor: وإني وإن كنت الأخير زمانه لآتت بما لم تستطعه الأوائل

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic line depicts a rider making an exclamation, placed in the discussion of the water drawer’s glad cry.
rows.anchor: يقول راكبه الجني مرتفقا هذا لكن ولحم الشاة محجور

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha describes a pearl diver exulting when he sees a pearl, illustrating the cry of delight at the discovery.
rows.anchor: أو درة صدفاته غواصها بهج متى يرها يهل ويسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding a boy in the well made Yusuf a foundling who belonged to whoever found him, which explains the water drawer’s joy.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : وجدت في البئر غلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ghulam is between ten and twenty years old; Yusuf was seventeen at the time.
rows.anchor: من سنه بين العشر والعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan were Ishmaelites according to the Torah; another view makes them people of Midian fetching water, while Yusuf’s brothers had moved away.
rows.anchor: كانوا من أهل مدين وكان مجيئهم الجب للاستقاء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asarruhu means the caravan concealed Yusuf and news of finding him, fearing nearby family would reclaim a boy who looked well-born.
rows.anchor: أخفوه . والضمير للسيارة لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty in a foundling case was to identify him publicly; their concealment suggests Yusuf told them his story and they suppressed it to sell him, from irreligion or failure to practice religion.
rows.anchor: وكان الشأن أن يعرفوا من كان قريبا من ذلك الجب ويعلنوا كما هو الشأن في التعريف باللقطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍāʿatan is an anticipatory circumstantial accusative from the object pronoun: they turned Yusuf into merchandise and resolved to sell him.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال المقدرة من الضمير المنصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge covers their wrongful enslavement of someone they had no right to enslave and their failure to find or return his family.
rows.anchor: من استرقاق من ليس لهم حق في استرقاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan’s discovery of Yusuf at the well is a sign of God’s gentle care for him.
rows.anchor: وفي عثور السيارة على الجب الذي فيه يوسف عليه السلام آية من لطف الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharayhu means they sold Yusuf; the basic verb denotes the act, while its iftiʿāl form marks the corresponding acquisition. Reading it as ‘bought’ misreads their lack of interest.
rows.anchor: يقال : شرى كما يقال : باع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the claim by some lexicographers that shara and ishtara are synonyms, finding no evidence for it.
rows.anchor: وما ادعاه بعض أهل اللغة أن شرى واشترى مترادفان في معنييهما يغلب على ظني أنه وهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakhs is an infinitive used here for something undervalued, like khalq for something created.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا بمعنى المبخوس كالخلق بمعنى المخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirham is a plural for the minted coin and a Persian loanword according to al-Jawhari; al-Suyuti’s catalogue of Quranic loanwords omitted it.
rows.anchor: وهو معرب عن الفارسية كما في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the coins ‘counted’ euphemistically means they were few, since small amounts are counted while large ones are weighed or measured.
rows.anchor: كناية عن كونها قليلة لأن الشيء القليل يسهل عده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronouns in the verse refer to the caravan, which Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the soundest interpretation.
rows.anchor: وضمائر الجمع كلها للسيارة على أصح التفاسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhd means little desire for the valued object or its price; the caravan did not seek a high price for Yusuf, perhaps because they knew little about prices.
rows.anchor: أي كان السيارة غير راغبين في إغلاء ثمن يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying they were among the indifferent is more emphatic than simply calling them indifferent: it places them among simple people who habitually undervalue rare things.
rows.anchor: أشد مبالغة مما لو أخبر بكانوا فيه زاهدين

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمازني
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr sides with al-Akhfash and al-Mazini: the definite article in al-zahidin is generic, not a relative pronoun as most grammarians claim.
rows.anchor: وخالفهم الأخفش والمازني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing fihi before its governor honors what the traders undervalued and highlights their weak discernment, while preserving the rhyme.
rows.anchor: وللتنبيه على ضعف توسمهم وبصارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The buyer is the person who paid and acquired ownership even if another person conducted the transaction; legal documents therefore specify for whom a purchase was made.
rows.anchor: مراد منه الذي دفع الثمن فملكه وإن كان لم يتول الاشتراء بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchaser was called Futifar, chief of Egypt’s royal police and governor of the city, later titled al-ʿAziz.
rows.anchor: رجل اسمه ( فوطيفار ) رئيس شرط ملك مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city of Egypt was Memphis in Lower Egypt, ruled by Canaanite Hyksos; Upper Egypt, centered on Thebes, remained under Coptic pharaohs and was weakened by Canaanite control.
rows.anchor: وهي قاعدة مصر السفلى التي يحكمها قبائل من الكنعانيين عرفوا عند القبط باسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic books call the wife Zuleikha, while Jewish sources call her Raʿil.
rows.anchor: وامرأته تسمى في كتب العرب ( زليخا ) بفتح الزاي وكسر اللام وقصر آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min Misr is an adjective describing the person who bought Yusuf.
rows.anchor: و { من مصر } صفة ل { الذي اشتراه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-imraʾatihi can attach to qala, ishtara, or both; attaching it to both suggests he bought Yusuf to give his wife as a son, implying they had no child.
rows.anchor: متعلق ب { قال } أو ب { اشتراه } أو يتنازعه كلا الفعلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imraʾah means wife here: the word for woman can denote a spouse.
rows.anchor: فإن الزوجة يطلق عليها اسم المرأة ويراد منه معنى الزوجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathwa literally means a place one returns to, but here it euphemistically means the quality of one’s stay; the order is to give Yusuf an excellent home.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا كناية عن حال الإقامة عندهما لأن المرء يثوى إلى منزل إقامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband hoped that kind treatment would win Yusuf’s affection and counsel, benefiting them, or lead them to adopt him so he would care for them; he may have despaired of having a child.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يجعل الإحسان إليه سببا في اجتلاب محبته إياهما ونصحه لهما فينفعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband likely read Yusuf’s promise of future excellence from his features; a cautious king would appoint only competent people as chief of police.
rows.anchor: لحسن تفرسه في ملامح يوسف عليه السلام المؤذنة بالكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, ‘thus’ points to the empowerment itself at its fullest attainable degree, with the comparison serving as an emphatic absolute object.
rows.anchor: كانت الإشارة إلى التمكين المستفاد من { مكنا ليوسف } تنويها بأن ذلك التمكين بلغ غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another reading, ‘thus’ refers to the miraculous rescue just described, with the phrase functioning circumstantially.
rows.anchor: وإن أجرينا على ما يحتمله اللفظ كانت لحاصل المذكور آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Empowerment here begins with Yusuf’s placement under the Aziz’s care; its fullest realization in 12:56 completes this opening and returns to it.
rows.anchor: فما ذكر هنالك هو كرد العجز على الصدر مما هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘to teach him’ gives the reason for God’s gift and empowerment: God saved Yusuf from death to prepare him to become a prophet skilled in dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: لما قدر في سابق علمه أن يجعل يوسف عليه السلام عالما بتأويل الرؤيا وأن يجعله نبيئا أنجاه من الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwil al-ahadith here means interpretation of dreams, as in Jacob’s promise to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: أي تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘God is dominant over His affair’ is a parenthetical general conclusion, including God’s defeat of the brothers’ plot; ‘His’ refers to God.
rows.anchor: لأن مفهومها عام يشمل غلب الله إخوة يوسف عليه السلام بإبطال كيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After verbs of prevailing, ʿala marks what is contested; God completes what He decreed, and no rival can prevent His will.
rows.anchor: بعد مادة الغلب ونحوها يدخل على الشيء الذي يتوقع فيه النزاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing qualification says most people fail to understand God’s assured completion of His plan even when its signs are evident.
rows.anchor: ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون ذلك مع ظهوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse announces that God chose Yusuf for prophethood, placed here after the account of his empowerment and teaching.
rows.anchor: هذا إخبار عن اصطفاء يوسف عليه السلام للنبوءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means strength and is interpreted as the ages thirty-five to forty.
rows.anchor: وفسر ببلوغه ما بين خمس وثلاثين سنة إلى أربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hukm and hikma are synonymous; here hukm is prophethood, while knowledge is an additional gift beyond prophethood, as with David and Solomon.
rows.anchor: وأريد به هنا النبوءة كما في قوله تعالى في ذكر داود وسليمان عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite tanwin in ʿilman marks a kind of knowledge or magnifies it; Ibn ʿĀshūr identifies it as dream interpretation.
rows.anchor: والمراد : علم تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: فخر الدين
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din distinguishes hukm as practical wisdom governing the self and ʿilm as theoretical wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقال فخر الدين : الحكم : الحكمة العملية لأنها حكم على هدى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of ‘thus We reward the good-doers’ follows the same pattern as the similar phrase in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: والقول في وكذلك نجزي المحسنين } كالقول في نظيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the good-doers hints that Yusuf’s excellence caused him to receive this blessing; God’s arrangement is a sign among those in Yusuf’s story.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أن إحسانه هو سبب جزائه بتلك النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next story need not have happened after the preceding one; the attempted seduction occurred before Yusuf’s prophethood, likely granted after his family arrived in Egypt and Jacob died.
rows.anchor: فلا يلزم أن تكون هذه القصة حاصلة في الوجود بعد التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage emphasizes Yusuf’s chastity, loyalty, and noble character.
rows.anchor: لتقرير ثبات يوسف عليه السلام على العفاف والوفاء وكرم الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Murawada’s reciprocal form conveys repeated attempts; another grammatical account treats the woman’s pursuit and Yusuf’s resistance as reciprocal action.
rows.anchor: والمفاعلة مستعملة في التكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Murawada derives from rada, going and coming; repeated approaches to a person are metaphorically called an attempt or persuasion.
rows.anchor: شبه حال المحاول أحدا على فعل شيء مكررا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction with ʿan is presented as Quranic innovation and makes the woman seek to turn Yusuf from himself and his control over his own will.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا التركيب من مبتكرات القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya reads nafs as Yusuf’s chastity and his capacity to yield himself to what she wanted.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عطية ، أي فالنفس أريد بها عفافه وتمكينها منه لما تريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ʿala, the verb instead takes the thing sought as its object; reports use it for urging Abu Talib to Islam and Moses persuading the Israelites.
rows.anchor: فذلك إلى الشيء المطلوب حصوله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet urging his uncle Abu Talib to accept Islam, illustrating rauda with ʿala.
rows.anchor: ووقع في قول أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يراود عمه أبا طالب على الإسلام

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: In the Isra report, Moses says he urged the Israelites to something less demanding and they abandoned it, another use of rauda with ʿala.
rows.anchor: فقال له موسى : قد والله راودت بني إسرائيل على أدنى من ذلك فتركوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling her ‘the one in whose house he was’ highlights Yusuf’s chastity because being in her household could have made compliance easier.
rows.anchor: لقصد ما تؤذن به الصلة من تقرير عصمة يوسف عليه السلام لأن كونه في بيتها من شأنه أن يطوعه لمرادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baytiha may mean the dwelling where she lived, or the whole palace and household of the owner, of which Yusuf was a member.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالبيت : المنزل كله ، وهو قصر العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghallaqat describes blocking each doorway; doubling the verb conveys forceful, thorough closure.
rows.anchor: لإفادة شدة الفعل وقوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bab is plural here, with an earlier Quranic usage cited for comparison.
rows.anchor: والأبواب : جمع باب . وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { ادخلوا عليهم الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayta is an imperative particle meaning ‘hurry’ and is attributed either to Hurrian/Nabataean or to Hebrew.
rows.anchor: قيل أصلها من اللغة الحورانية ، وهي نبطية . وقيل : هي من اللغة العبرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The li in laka clarifies the addressee and appears to be extra; the underlying form is haytak.
rows.anchor: لزيادة بيان المقصود بالخطاب ، كما في قولهم : سقيا لك وشكرا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr suggests she began with an immediate offer because palace custom may have allowed a woman to enjoy her male slave as a man did a female slave.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أنها طلبت منه أمرا كان غير بدع في قصورهم بأن تستمتع المرأة بعبدها

rows.speaker: نافع وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Dhakwan from Ibn ʿAmir, and Abu Jaʿfar read hayta with kasra on ha and fatḥa on ta.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع ، وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر بكسر الهاء وفتح المثناة الفوقية

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads hayta with fatḥa on ha, a still ya, and ḍamma on ta.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير بفتح الهاء وسكون التحتية وضم الفوقية

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the same stated opening and final vowel pattern; the fatḥa and ḍamma are inflectional vowels of an indeclinable form.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الباقون بفتح الهاء وسكون التحتية وضم التاء الفوقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿadh is a verbal noun annexed to God as its object, meaning ‘I seek refuge in God’ from her attempt.
rows.anchor: مصدر أضيف إلى اسم الجلالة إضافة المصدر إلى معموله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna explains the refusal and refuge as prompted by God’s command to seek protection.
rows.anchor: تعليل ما أفاده معاذ الله } من الامتناع والاعتصام منه بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbi may refer to God as Creator, or to her husband as master and owner, a double reading suited to Yusuf’s artful refusal.
rows.anchor: وضمير { إنه } يجوز أن يعود إلى اسم الجلالة ، ويكون { ربي } بمعنى خالقي . ويجوز أن يعود إلى معلوم من المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s concise wording either reproduces Yusuf’s Egyptian phrasing or compresses two reasons for refusal: God’s command and loyalty to his master.
rows.anchor: حكي به كلام يوسف عليه السلام إما لأن يوسف عليه السلام أتى بمثل هذا التركيب في لغة القبط

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda reads the clause as an advanced response and delayed condition: Yusuf would have desired her had he not seen his Lord’s proof.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : هذا على التقديم والتأخير

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari objects that the response to lawla cannot precede the condition.
rows.anchor: وطعن في هذا التأويل الطبري بأن جواب { لولا } لا يتقدم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr answers that Abu ʿUbayda accepts an advanced response, or the preceding clause can signal an omitted response; some omission is required on every reading.
rows.anchor: ويدفع هذا الطعن أن أبا عبيدة لما قال ذلك علمنا أنه لا يرى منع تقديم جواب { لولا }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن أبي مليكة وثعلب
rows.claim: One group says Yusuf intended to answer her invitation, then recoiled at the proof; divine protection made him desist, and a restrained sinful intention is not a major sin.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ، وقتادة ، وابن أبي مليكة ، وثعلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This view is compatible with the majority position that prophets are protected from major sins even before prophethood, though that doctrine is disputed; Ibn ʿAbbas allowed it for Yusuf.
rows.anchor: ولذلك جوز ابن عباس ذلك على يوسف

rows.speaker: السدي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and a report from Ibn ʿAbbas say Yusuf intended the act and began preparing, then saw the proof and stopped; Ibn ʿĀshūr treats this as equivalent to the preceding view.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول السدي ، ورواية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr criticizes al-Kashshaf for attributing the reports to ‘Hashwiyya’ and ‘Mujbira’ as a smear against Ashʿaris while ignoring the named transmitters.
rows.anchor: وقد خبط صاحب ( الكشاف ) في إلصاق هذه الروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the proof is intellectual apprehension because a proof is abstract, not visible to the eye.
rows.anchor: الرؤية : هنا علمية لأن البرهان من المعاني التي لا ترى بالبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof was God’s intervention blocking Yusuf’s desire; without it, her beauty, wish, pleasure in pleasing her, closeness, and youth would have stirred human inclination.
rows.anchor: ولولا ذلك لكان حال البشرية لا يسلم من الهم بمطاوعتها في تلك الحالة لتوفر دواعي الهم من حسنها

rows.speaker: مفسرون غير مسمين
rows.claim: Commentators variously identify the proof as a rational argument, divine revelation, divine protection, or visions made visible to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من يشير إلى أنه حجة نظرية قبحت له هذا الفعل ، وقيل : هو وحي إلهي ، وقيل : حفظ إلهي ، وقيل : مشاهدات تمثلت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Thus, to turn away’ refers back to Yusuf’s seeing the proof and explains why God showed it to him.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في قوله : { كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء } إلى شيء مفهوم مما قبله بتضمنه قوله : { رأى برهان ربه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarf literally means moving something between places; here it metaphorically means protecting Yusuf from evil and lewdness, whose causes were present.
rows.anchor: والصرف : نقل الشيء من مكان إلى مكان ، وهو هنا مجاز عن الحفظ من حلول الشيء بالمحل الذي من شأنه أن يحل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawʾ is betrayal of trust, while fahshaʾ is sin, specifically adultery.
rows.anchor: والسوء : القبيح ، وهو خيانة من ائتمنه . والفحشاء : المعصية ، وهي الزنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among God’s chosen servants explains the extraordinary protection and preserves Yusuf’s status as one selected by God.
rows.anchor: تعليل لحكمة صرفه عن السوء والفحشاء الصرف الخارق للعادة لئلا ينتقص اصطفاء الله إياه

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف
rows.claim: These readers pronounce al-mukhlasin with an open lam, meaning those whom God chose; another reader group pronounces it with a kasra, meaning those who are sincere to God, with the same explanatory force.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع ، وعاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وأبو جعفر ، وخلف { المخلصين } بفتح اللام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce al-mukhlisin with a kasra, meaning those sincere in their religion for God.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وابن عامر ، ويعقوب بكسر اللام على معنى المخلصين دينهم لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istibaq means competing to be first; both Yusuf and the woman tried to reach the door first.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا إشارة إلى تكلفهما السبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bab is accusative after omission of ila, or because istabaqa incorporates the sense of ibtadara.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { الباب } على نزع الخافض . وأصله : واستبقا إلى الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic definite ‘door’ represents the several locked doors: Yusuf fled toward them to open them while she tried to block his escape.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في ( الباب ) تعريف الجنس إذ كانت عدة أبواب مغلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt was torn before the race; a tear from behind shows she seized Yusuf as he turned away and he pulled free, whereas a tear during the race would prove little.
rows.anchor: وذلك قبل الاستباق لا محالة . لأنه لو كان تمزيق القميص في حال الاستباق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise phrase combines the race, the torn shirt, and the inference of Yusuf’s flight and her attempt to restrain him.
rows.anchor: وقد أبدع إيجاز الآية في جمع هذه المعاني تحت جملة { استبقا الباب وقدت قميصه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They unexpectedly found her husband, the Aziz, at the outer doorway as he entered the house.
rows.anchor: وصادف أن ألفيا سيدها ، أي زوجها ، وهو العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a husband sayyid likely reflects Egyptian usage of that period, unlike Arabic usage; Ibn ʿĀshūr sees this as a historical detail and links the phrase to the king’s law.
rows.anchor: فالتعبير به هنا من دقائق التاريخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies Yusuf opened the doors she had locked one by one while they raced to the outer door, an event compressed by the narrative.
rows.anchor: وقد علم من الكلام أن يوسف عليه السلام فتح الأبواب التي غلقتها زليخا بابا بابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilfaʾ is to find something in a particular state without seeking it, often unexpectedly or without knowing when it first appeared.
rows.anchor: والإلفاء : وجدان شيء على حالة خاصة من غير سعي لوجدانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife’s question about punishment is a new explanatory sentence prompted by the listener’s question about what happened at the door.
rows.anchor: وجملة قالت ما جزاء } الخ مستأنفة بيانيا ، لأن السامع يسأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She spoke first with brazen deception and framed her accusation as a general rule to make her husband accept it; she feared his affection for Yusuf and sought to hide her desire and intimidate Yusuf from resisting later.
rows.anchor: وابتدرته بالكلام إمعانا في البهتان بحيث لم تتلعثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife offers prison or another painful punishment; confinement was an ancient penalty still known in Moses’ time, as Pharaoh’s threat shows.
rows.anchor: وكان الحبس عقابا قديما في ذلك العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other torment could mean beating, burning, or cutting off limbs, and the narrative will mention prison repeatedly.
rows.anchor: ومنه الضرب والإيلام بالنار وبقطع الأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s ‘she pursued me’ is separated as dialogue; placing the subject before the verb restricts the blame to her and answers her accusation.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المبتدأ على خبره الذي هو فعل يفيد القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ‘that he be imprisoned’ is clearer than a noun for prison because sijn can name either the act or the building.
rows.anchor: لأن لفظ السجن يطلق على البيت الذي يوضع فيه المسجون ويطلق على مصدر سجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness was a perceptive relative of the woman; his test is circumstantial evidence, since a front tear would fit her account of holding Yusuf for punishment, but a rear tear fits his flight.
rows.anchor: وكان مع العزيز رجل من أهل امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt counts as testimony because it establishes or defeats the charge; the witness inferred the tear from the wife’s own mention of it.
rows.anchor: وسمي قوله شهادة لأنه يؤول إلى إظهار الحق في إثبات اعتداء يوسف عليه السلام على سيدته أو دحضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness likely believed the wife and tried to prove her allegation, but the evidence reversed the case as a divine favor to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الشاهد كان يظن صدقها فأراد أن يقيم دليلا على صدقها فوقع عكس ذلك كرامة ليوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional test explains what the witness testified.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن كان قميصه } مبينة لفعل { شهد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added clauses ‘she is among the liars’ and ‘he is among the truthful’ reinforce the ruling’s truth.
rows.anchor: وزيادة { وهو من الكاذبين } بعد { فصدقت } ، وزيادة { وهو من الصادقين } بعد { فكذبت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conditional particles express connection and consequence without fixing tense; here they describe an already completed tear and its past implication.
rows.anchor: وأدوات الشرط لا تدل على أكثر من الربط والتسبب بين مضمون شرطها ومضمون جوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker who saw the rear tear and called it the women’s scheme was the Aziz; he knew Yusuf was innocent and addressed the wife in a plural generalization about women.
rows.anchor: والذي رأى قميصه قد من دبر وقال : إنه من كيدكن ، هو العزيز لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaid is an act disguised as one thing in order to reach a different goal.
rows.anchor: والكيد : فعل شيء في صورة غير المقصودة للتوصل إلى مقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf is told to leave the matter alone, meaning not punish her or reopen the accusation; she must seek forgiveness for accusing him of aggression.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر يوسف عليه السلام بالإعراض عما رمته به

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say the Aziz was either not jealous or was patient and sensible; perhaps he doted on his wife, or royal status softened accountability for her pursuit of a slave.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : وكان العزيز قليل الغيرة . وقيل : كان حليما عاقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭiʾ means one who commits a crime; placing her among offenders softens the rebuke, and the masculine plural is generic.
rows.anchor: والخاطىء : فاعل الخطيئة ، وهي الجريمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz speaks as the judicial authority; after addressing Yusuf, the coordinated command shifts to the wife, as shown by the feminine pronoun.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يوسف أعرض عن هذا } من قول العزيز إذ هو صاحب الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niswa is a feminine collective noun without a singular, like nisaʾ; the locative phrase indicates women scattered through Memphis and news circulating among households connected to the Aziz.
rows.anchor: النسوة : اسم جمع امرأة لا مفرد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wife confided in friends who spread the secret, either to consult them or relieve herself by speaking about what she loved; later verses support this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن امرأة العزيز باحت بالسر لبعض خلائلها فأفشينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fata means a young man and euphemistically a slave or servant; Yusuf is called hers because he belonged to her husband and was therefore her servant by marriage.
rows.anchor: ويكنى به عن المملوك وعن الخادم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaghaf derives from the heart’s outer covering and means love penetrated her heart; hubban specifies the relation, whose underlying sense is that Yusuf’s love reached her heart.
rows.anchor: وشغف : فعل مشتق من اسم جامد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb qāla can be masculine with a plural noun like niswat, just as the Quran says a caravan came; the final tāʾ in niswat is part of a broken-plural pattern, not feminine marking.
rows.anchor: وتذكير الفعل في { وقال نسوة } لأن الفعل المسند إلى ألفاظ الجموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz’s name and the Arabic and Hebrew names of his wife were given in the earlier discussion of Yusuf’s purchase.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم وجه تسمية الذي اشترى يوسف عليه السلام باسم العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense turawidu depicts the past seduction as if occurring now to emphasize its strange and blameworthy character.
rows.anchor: بصيغة المضارع مع كون المراودة مضت لقصد استحضار الحالة العجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘She is consumed with love’ gives the reason for her pursuing the servant.
rows.anchor: في موضع التعليل لجملة { تراود فتاها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic opening of ‘we see her in manifest error’ establishes the women’s judgment and disclaims jealousy as their motive.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد ب ( إن ) واللام لتحقيق اعتقادهن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dalal here means departure from sound judgment through infatuation, not religious error, as in the brothers’ earlier accusation about Jacob.
rows.anchor: والضلال هنا : مخالفة طريق الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing is normally transitive directly; the bi here either means ‘be told about,’ as in the proverb about the Maʿidi, or is emphatic like the Quranic example.
rows.anchor: فتعديته بالباء هنا إما لأنه ضمن معنى أخبرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their speech is called scheming because they wanted the news to reach her and prompt her to display Yusuf, whom they wanted to see.
rows.anchor: لأنهن أردن بذلك أن يبلغ قولهن إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they spoke secretly, making their talk resemble a plot.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأنهن قلنه خفية فأشبه المكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that they feigned disapproval while inwardly envying her; desiring a male slave may not have been condemned in their custom.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أطلق على قولهن اسم المكر لأنهن قلنه في صورة الإنكار وهن يضمرن حسدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtadat derives from aʿdadt with the first dal changed to ta, as discussed in al-Nisaʾ.
rows.anchor: أصله أعددت ، أبدلت الدال الأولى تاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muttakaʾ is a reclining place; reclining is a restful, near-lying posture for a long meal, a luxury custom known to Romans and evidenced by surviving couches.
rows.anchor: والاتكاء : جلسة قريبة من الاضطجاع على الجنب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said that he does not eat while reclining.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي : أما أنا فلا آكل متكئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘She gave them’ means that she ordered her servants to provide the cushions, as with the command to Haman.
rows.anchor: أمرت خدمها بالإيتاء كقوله : { يا هامان ابن لي صرحا

rows.speaker: قائلون
rows.claim: It is said she served citron and bananas, then the women reclined; the fruit and seating actions are omitted, and each received a knife to peel fruit.
rows.anchor: قيل : أحضرت لهن أترجا وموزا فحضرن واتكأن ، وقد حذف هذان الفعلان إيجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Come out to them’ implies Yusuf was in another room and entered only with permission; ʿala is used because the intended action is entering upon them.
rows.anchor: يقتضي أنه كان في بيت آخر وكان لا يدخل عليها إلا بإذنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akbarnahu means they found his beauty and qualities extraordinary; greatness of qualities is pictured as greatness of body.
rows.anchor: أي أعظمن جماله وشمائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women cut their hands from distraction as they ran knives over them while thinking they were cutting fruit; ‘cut’ figuratively intensifies the wound.
rows.anchor: أي أجرين السكاكين على أيديهن يحسبن أنهن يقطعن الفواكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasha lillah is an Arabic fixed expression for negation and declaring something free of blame; its base denotes distancing and can function as an oath-like denial invoking God.
rows.anchor: وأصل ( حاشا ) فعل يدل على المباعدة عن شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase with li can mean they keep God from falsehood for His sake or out of fear of Him; the Egyptian utterance is rendered by meaning.
rows.anchor: بحذف الألف ، أي حاشا لأجله ، أي لخوفه أن أكذب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr retains the alif in hasha lillah when connecting words; the other readers omit it, and everyone omits it at pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ( حاشا لله ) بإثبات ألف حاشا في الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘This is no human’ exaggerates that Yusuf surpasses human beauty; they then make an emphatic, eloquent comparison by restricting him to the class of angels.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في فوته محاسن البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women’s emphatic simile restricts Yusuf to the angelic class, comparing him to an angel.
rows.anchor: ثم شبهنه بواحد من الملائكة بطريقة حصره في جنس الملائكة تشبيها بليغا مؤكدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptians believed in celestial spiritual beings and judgment-day judges, sometimes represented beautifully; ‘noble angel’ approximates in Arabic a being like what they imagined.
rows.anchor: وكان القبط يعتقدون وجود موجودات علوية هي من جنس الأرواح العلوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in ‘that is he’ is explanatory: if Yusuf is as you claim an angel, he is the man for whom you blamed me.
rows.anchor: والفاء في { فذلكن } فاء الفصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi in ‘you blamed me over him’ is causal, with an omitted noun meaning the matter or love of him; a hadith uses the same causal fi.
rows.anchor: ( في ) للتعليل ، مثل ( دخلت امرأة النار في هرة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhalikunna distinguishes Yusuf, whom the women had not seen; the relative phrase identifies him by the only description they knew, and she admitted pursuing him once she saw their infatuation.
rows.anchor: والإشارة ب ( ذلكن ) لتمييز يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaʿṣama is an intensive form meaning Yusuf strongly protected himself, as with other verbs formed using s and t.
rows.anchor: فالسين والتاء للمبالغة ، مثل : استمسك واستجمع الرأي واستجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He refused as one protected from sin, treating the woman’s advances as wrongdoing from which he guarded himself.
rows.anchor: أنه امتنع امتناع معصوم ، أي جاعلا المراودة خطيئة عصم نفسه منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She remained intent on seduction, asserted her status and command, and emphasized the prison threat with the nuns to frighten Yusuf in his hearing.
rows.anchor: فأكدت حصول سجنه بنوني التوكيد ، وقد قالت ذلك بمسمع منه إرهابا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause in ma amuruhu omits a pronoun governed by bi through removal of the preposition, as in amartuka al-khayr.
rows.anchor: وحذف عائد صلة { ما آمره } وهو ضمير مجرور بالباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, sijn is the regular verbal noun for imprisonment and is attested by Ibn ʿĀshūr only in Yaʿqub’s reading here; with kasra it names the prison building.
rows.anchor: ولم أره في كلامهم بفتح السين إلا في قراءة يعقوب هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saghir means humiliated; min al-saghirin is stronger than simply calling Yusuf humiliated, as shown in two earlier verses.
rows.anchor: وتركيب من الصاغرين } أقوى في معنى الوصف بالصغار من أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s answer responds to the two prisoners’ speech and is separated as a new turn in the dialogue.
rows.anchor: جواب عن كلامهما ففصلت على أسلوب حكاية جمل التحاور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He uses their attention while they await dream interpretation to invite them to true faith, promising an answer soon at the predictable time prison food arrives.
rows.anchor: أراد بهذا الجواب أن يفترص إقبالهما عليه وملازمة الحديث معه إذ هما يترقبان تعبيره الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food was a useful time marker in prison, where walls and closed doors blocked the sun and meals, sleep, or wind marked the day; the wording suggests the food was due soon.
rows.anchor: ولأن انطباق الأبواب وإحاطة الجدران يحول بينهم وبين رؤية الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it food they are provided with specifies a regularly timed ration, not an unpredictable gift.
rows.anchor: تصريح بالضبط بأنه طعام معلوم الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq means what benefits someone and can denote food, customary spending, or a regular stipend; the Quran uses it for food and provision in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الرزق : ما به النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘its interpretation’ refers to what the earlier pronoun referred to—the dream—not food; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the majority’s reading as types of food cannot aptly be called taʾwil.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي أن يعود إلى طعام إذ لا يحسن إطلاق التأويل عن الأنباء بأسماء أصناف الطعام خلافا لما سلكه جمهور المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception contrasts the relevant states of interpreting and not interpreting the dreams: the ration will not arrive without Yusuf first giving their interpretation, a contextually limited restriction.
rows.anchor: أي لا يأتي الطعام المعتاد إلا في حال أني قد نبأتكما بتأويل رؤياكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A past circumstantial clause can omit the waw when the exception itself links it, as in the Quranic example from al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: مع أنها ماضية اكتفاء بربط الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God taught Yusuf explains the promised interpretation and anticipates questions about how he gained such knowledge, leading into his call to monotheism; Egyptians were polytheists.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني ، لأن وعده بتأويل الرؤيا في وقت قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s teaching also hints that Yusuf had law, wisdom, economics, and trustworthiness beyond dream interpretation, as his later request to manage the storehouses shows.
rows.anchor: إيذان بأنه علمه علوما أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His declaration that he left the people’s religion further explains God’s favor and may also function as its cause: he alone upheld monotheism among the city’s polytheists.
rows.anchor: فأخبر بأن سبب عناية الله به أنه انفرد في ذلك المكان بتوحيد الله وترك ملة أهل المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Milla means religion, as in the expression about Abraham’s upright religion.
rows.anchor: والملة : الدين ، تقدم في قوله : { دينا قيما ملة إبراهيم حنيفا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people may include the Canaanites among whom Yusuf grew up and the Copts among whom he lived, or refer only to Canaanites while indirectly reproaching the similarly polytheistic Egyptians.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالقوم الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ما يشمل الكنعانيين الذين نشأ فيهم والقبط الذين شب بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic pronoun in ‘they are disbelievers’ singles out Canaanites, who rejected resurrection like Arab pagans; Copts were polytheists but believed in resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: أراد به تخصيص قوم منهم بذلك وهم الكنعانيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tark means leaving something one could adopt; Yusuf says he did not follow the Egyptians’ religion despite living among them under a master who followed it.
rows.anchor: أشار به إلى أنه لم يتبع ملة القبط مع حلوله بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning his fathers honors their virtue and shows that righteousness and knowledge characterized Yusuf from childhood, then were strengthened by God’s teaching.
rows.anchor: وذكر آباءه تعليما بفضلهم ، وإظهارا لسابقية الصلاح فيه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet named Yusuf son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham as a prophet descended from prophets; Ibn ʿĀshūr says this prophetic lineage is unique on certain definitions.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما سئل عن أكرم الناس : ( يوسف بن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following his fathers may mean adopting their foundations before prophethood, with dream interpretation and economics as additional revelation, or receiving a revelation like theirs, as in al-Shura.
rows.anchor: أو أن نبوءته كانت بوحي مثل ما أوحي به إلى آبائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking righteous ancestors strengthens a true claim, while mentioning ancestors in error prevents their practice from serving as proof, as the next verse explains.
rows.anchor: وذكر السلف الصالح في الحق يزيد دليل الحق تمكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic denial explains the preceding lineage: monotheism was a defining inherited trait, and the construction strongly rules out associating anything with God.
rows.anchor: في قوة البيان لما اقتضته جملة { واتبعت ملة آبائي } من كون التوحيد صار كالسجية لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr argues that historical evidence shows Coptic religion was polytheistic; historians’ attempts to reduce the gods to symbols still leave lesser deities under one supreme power, a common pattern rooted in imagined royal hierarchies.
rows.anchor: وكانت ديانة القبط في سائر العصور التي حفظها التاريخ وشهدت بها الآثار ديانة شرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptian religion associated gods with powers, elements, and celestial bodies; Greeks were similar and, in his comparison, better than Arab stone worship and Mesopotamian star worship.
rows.anchor: نعم إن القبط بنوا تعدد الآلهة على تعدد القوى والعناصر وبعض الكواكب ذات القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line about Thaqif’s flight to its goddess illustrates Arab tribal idol worship.
rows.anchor:
كما قال الشاعر :
وفرت ثقيف إلى لاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian pantheon numbered about thirty gods, including Amun-Ra, Osiris, Isis, and Horus; the Quran’s phrase ‘several scattered lords’ aptly conveys this multiplicity.
rows.anchor: وكانت آلهة القبط نحوا من ثلاثين ربا أكبرها عندهم آمون رع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After questioning whether the many gods are truly divine, Yusuf moves to deny that they have real referents at all, reducing them to invented names.
rows.anchor: وبعد أن أثار لهما الشك في صحة إلهية آلهتهم المتعددين انتقل إلى إبطال وجود تلك الآلهة على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You and your fathers’ explains who named the supposed gods, refuting ancestral authority while gently making it easier for the prisoners to abandon them.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من ذلك الرد على آبائهم سدا لمنافذ الاحتجاج لأحقيتها بأن تلك الآلهة معبودات آبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending down a sultan is a metaphor for creating evidence of divinity among the signs of the world; sultan means proof.
rows.anchor: وإنزال السلطان : كناية عن إيجاد دليل إلهيتها في شواهد العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Judgment belongs only to God’ denies the supposed powers and authority of the other gods.
rows.anchor: إبطال لجميع التصرفات المزعومة لآلهتهم بأنها لا حكم لها فيما زعموا أنه من حكمها وتصرفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship God alone turns from proof of His exclusive divinity to the duty of obeying His command, explaining the meaning of His judgment.
rows.anchor: انتقال من أدلة إثبات انفراد الله تعالى بالإلهية إلى التعليم بامتثال أمره ونهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing declaration summarizes the argument: this alone is the upright religion, returning rhetorically to Yusuf’s earlier statement that he left the people’s religion.
rows.anchor: خلاصة لما تقدم من الاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to Yusuf presupposes omitted words and omits the messenger’s sending, journey, and arrival because they do not advance the story, a concise narrative technique.
rows.anchor: الخطاب بالنداء مؤذن بقول محذوف في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siddiq derives as an intensive form from truthfulness and became a title for comprehensive virtue and upright obedience, qualities grounded in fidelity to religion.
rows.anchor: وأحسن ما رأيت في هذا المعنى كلمة الراغب الأصفهاني

rows.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines the siddiqun as the rank immediately below the prophets.
rows.anchor: كلمة الراغب الأصفهاني في مفردات القرآن قال : ( الصديقون هم دوين الأنبياء )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet called Abu Bakr a siddiq in the report addressing Mount Uhud, and Ibn ʿĀshūr cites the Companions’ consensus, including ʿAli, that Abu Bakr was the community’s best after the Prophet.
rows.anchor: في حديث رجف جبل أحد أسكن أحد فإنما عليك نبيء وصديق وشهيدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran also joins the descriptions siddiq and prophet for Idris, and the word can carry its basic sense of truthful believer in one reading of another verse.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما لقب النبيء أبا بكر بالصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prison companion calls Yusuf siddiq based on his evident truth and conduct, learned through personal experience of living with him.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصفه به عن خبرة وتجربة اكتسبها من مخالطة يوسف عليه السلام في السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the king’s exact words shows that the messenger delivered the question faithfully.
rows.anchor: وإعادة العبارات المحكية عن الملك بعينها إشارة إلى أنه بلغ السؤال كما تلقاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nas can mean some people rather than everyone; here it refers to the king and his council, all concerned with the dream’s interpretation and with Yusuf’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { الناس } بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘so they may know’ is omitted because each listener can infer what the king and courtiers need to learn.
rows.anchor: مع حذف معمول { يعلمون } لأن كل أحد يعلم ما يفيده علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence indicates that the speaker is the wife, continuing her confession; ‘I do not acquit myself’ guards against reading her earlier defense as a total claim of innocence, since she attempted the sin but was prevented.
rows.anchor: ظاهر ترتيب الكلام أن هذا من كلام امرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening waw is resumptive and the sentence begins a new statement.
rows.anchor: فالواو التي في الجملة استئنافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the soul strongly urges evil explains why she does not claim innocence.
rows.anchor: وجلمة { إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء } تعليل لجملة { وما أبرىء نفسي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception concerns times of evil: God’s mercy protects by providing a deterrent or obstacle, as Yusuf’s refusal prevented her from committing the sin, a kindness to both.
rows.anchor: استثناء من عموم الأزمان ، أي أزمان وقوع السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending praises God’s extensive forgiveness for sinners and mercy in turning a servant away from sin.
rows.anchor: ثناء على الله بأنه شديد المغفرة لمن أذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her statement implies that her people believed in God and prohibited wrongdoing; this is compatible with polytheism, as Arab idolaters also believed God created the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن قومها يؤمنون بالله ويحرمون الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her public admission before the king teaches the virtue of acknowledging truth, clearing an innocent person, and fearing God’s punishment of traitors.
rows.anchor: وفي اعتراف امرأة العزيز بحضرة الملك عبرة بفضيلة الاعتراف بالحق

rows.speaker: قائلون
rows.claim: Another view makes these Yusuf’s words, continuing his request that the king investigate the women who cut their hands.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هذا الكلام كلام يوسف عليه السلام متصل بقوله : ارجع إلى ربك
